messages:
alex: FYI I uploaded santorini-13b v1 to s3://redwood-models/santorini/13b/v1. Layout is under that prefix (pytorch_model.bin, config.json, tokenizer files). Can someone validate the artifact shape and loader config before I run the full perf matrix?
priya: I will. quick check: do we have merges.txt + vocab, or is this the HF fast tokenizer bundle? saw emoji splitting issues last time.
josh: It's the fast tokenizer bundle (tokenizer.json + merges). Note: I reproduced an odd split for repeated trophies "🏆🏆" where the fast build inserted a stray filler token. Repro: 
```bash
python -c "from tokenizers import Tokenizer; t=Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json'); print(t.encode('🏆🏆').tokens)"
```
mel: Also spotted a mismatch: model_config.yaml lists rotary_dim: 64 but the checkpoint metadata says 32. Loader validation fails with KV_CACHE shape mismatch. I put a tiny fix up in the model-config branch to align fields.
alex: Good catch. priya/josh can you confirm tokenizer normalizer/merges so we don't get surprise tokenization drift? If emoji/ZWJ sequences break we should add overrides in the catalog entry.
priya: Quick diff: merges.txt is present but tokenizer.json lacks an explicit "normalizer" section. When we hydrate with HF tokenizer it defaults differently. Proposed quick patch: inject a minimal normalizer config (NFD) and re-export.
josh: Sounds right. For perf runs, plan matrix: batch_sizes [1,4,8,16], seq_lens [128,512], kv_cache [true,false], quant [fp16,int8]. Also test workers=1 isolated for p50/p95 latency.
ci-bot: perf-run queued: santorini-13b v1  matrix: batches=[1,4,8,16], seq=[128,512], kv_cache=[true,false], quant=[fp16,int8]. Job id: prf-1742 :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
deploy-bot: artifact santorini-13b:v1 uploaded to staging registry (sha: a1b2c3).
priya: After adding normalizer I re-ran the tokenizers check. Tokens for "🏆🏆" -> ["🏆", "🏆"] now, no filler token. pushed commit to branch catalog/santorini-tokenizer-fix. :thumbsup:
mel: I updated model-config.yaml to rotary_dim: 32 and added tokenizer_overrides: {normalizer: 'nfd'} in the draft catalog entry. pushed to catalog/santorini-13b branch.
alex: Nice. When CI results arrive can someone paste p50/p95 for single-batch (batch=1) seq=128 kv_cache=true so I can compare to mosaic7b baseline?
josh: Will run isolated harness and paste results. Using this command: 
```bash
./tools/bench_infer --model s3://redwood-models/santorini/13b/v1 --batch 1 --seq 128 --kv_cache true --quant fp16 --workers 1 --warmup 50 --iters 200
```
priya: My quick warmup on an a100-80: p50 82ms, p95 210ms (batch=1 seq=128 fp16 kv_cache=true, single GPU).
josh: That's a bit above expectations (mosaic7b p50 ~60ms). Looking at runtime logs now, I see attention kernel fallback to slower path for some sequences. snippet: 
``n[2025-11-05T14:12:03Z] INFO kernel_selector: selected attention_kernel=scaled_dot_product_v2_fallback
[2025-11-05T14:12:03Z] WARN runtime: falling back to slower kernel due to seq_len pattern
```
mel: CI perf dashboard shows good tokens/s for batch>=8 but we need per-config latency traces. I added link to the job in the perf dashboard.
alex: Action list: (1) merge mel's config fix, (2) priya finalize tokenizer commit and include normalizer, (3) josh run isolated latency test and attach logs, (4) update catalog entry with tokenizer_overrides + validated S3 paths. I'll request CR on the catalog PR once ready.
josh: done a quick isolated run. attaching condensed log and p50/p95: p50 86ms, p95 228ms (a100-80, fp16, kv_cache=true, batch=1). attaching attention trace.
priya: I can run a padding/packing trace to confirm if padding distribution causes kernel fallback. will post histogram.
alex: Good. Also add a short note to #model-catalog onboarding checklist about emoji/ZWJ handling and verifying rotary_dim vs checkpoint metadata so future imports don't miss this. :memo:
ci-bot: perf-run prf-1742 completed: summary posted to perf dashboard (job prf-1742). Link: https://perf.internal/redwood/prf-1742
josh: CI job artifacts include the kernel selector logs and the full traces. I'll paste the critical lines into this thread once I parse them.
mel: If kernel fallback is sequence-pattern dependent, maybe a mix of packed batches + slight sequence bucketing will avoid fallbacks. worth trying before we consider model-level changes.
alex: Agreed. let's reconvene async here once josh posts final traces. thanks all for quick turn.
